table.text: The protocol was approved by Northeastern University's Institutional Review Board 19-03-20.
Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog).

In the present two-arm randomized feasibility trial, participants completed an 8-week audiovisual intervention that is designed to rehabilitate neural oscillations using a combination of musical rhythms and synchronized light pulses (see Figure 1A for example of device used for light stimulation).

table.text: Participants completed both protocols at high rates, and the treatment group listened for longer than the control group.
We recruited adults aged 50 to 90 from the metropolitan Boston area through paid advertisements and community outreach events.
Of the 155 assessed, 91 were excluded, and the remaining 64 were randomized into the two intervention protocols (treatment and control).
Two were enrolled through a scoring error on the prescreen and did not meet criteria for MCI.
Nineteen participants completed the treatment protocol and 19 completed the control protocol.
EEG data were collected for 34 participants and 33 out of 38 participants had both behavioral performance and EEG.
After determining eligibility, participants completed a pre-intervention assessment in the laboratory to establish a baseline on neuropsychological and neuroimaging measures.
Prior to random assignment to one of two intervention protocols, participants completed a series of pre-intervention assessments in the lab.
The pre-intervention session took approximately 7 hours to complete and participants were compensated $20 per hour.
The behavioral assessments and neuroimaging tasks completed by participants are outlined below.
Immediately after the final encoding block, participants were tested on 14 of the studied faces, 12 novel and 2 repeated.
Participants had 6.65 s to respond with a button press.
Data from one treatment-group participant were lost to equipment failure, leaving 37 participants for the face-name analyses.
In the Maze task, participants completed a series of mazes.
Participants were asked to listen for at least 30 minutes a day across the eight weeks while viewing the light stimulation, choosing one of the two playlists each day.
The post-intervention session took approximately 7 hours, and participants were compensated $20 per hour.
Compliance measures came from the daily logbooks which participants completed by hand after each session.
Logbook data are incomplete for four participants who completed the intervention and remained in contact with research staff throughout.

We then compared the delta-theta-gamma-driven light stimulation to the delta-driven light stimulation on delta, theta, and gamma gain, and on theta phase-locking value, using a paired cluster-based permutation test across the 30 electrodes, with each participant's values averaged across the two songs (n = 33; one participant had no delta-driven recording for one song and was excluded from these tests).
We asked whether our music and synchronized light stimulus entrained endogenous brain oscillations in our participants.
Participants completed a battery of neuropsychological measures at both sessions, drawn from several instruments rather than from a single published battery.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

summary_table.ethics_statements: The protocol was approved by Northeastern University's Institutional Review Board 19-03-20.
live_data_statements: Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog).

In the present two-arm randomized feasibility trial, participants completed an 8-week audiovisual intervention that is designed to rehabilitate neural oscillations using a combination of musical rhythms and synchronized light pulses (see Figure 1A for example of device used for light stimulation).
Participants completed both protocols at high rates, and the treatment group listened for longer than the control group.
We recruited adults aged 50 to 90 from the metropolitan Boston area through paid advertisements and community outreach events.
Of the 155 assessed, 91 were excluded, and the remaining 64 were randomized into the two intervention protocols (treatment and control).
Two were enrolled through a scoring error on the prescreen and did not meet criteria for MCI.
Nineteen participants completed the treatment protocol and 19 completed the control protocol.
EEG data were collected for 34 participants and 33 out of 38 participants had both behavioral performance and EEG.
After determining eligibility, participants completed a pre-intervention assessment in the laboratory to establish a baseline on neuropsychological and neuroimaging measures.
Prior to random assignment to one of two intervention protocols, participants completed a series of pre-intervention assessments in the lab.
The pre-intervention session took approximately 7 hours to complete and participants were compensated $20 per hour.
The behavioral assessments and neuroimaging tasks completed by participants are outlined below.
Immediately after the final encoding block, participants were tested on 14 of the studied faces, 12 novel and 2 repeated.
Participants had 6.65 s to respond with a button press.
Data from one treatment-group participant were lost to equipment failure, leaving 37 participants for the face-name analyses.
In the Maze task, participants completed a series of mazes.
Participants were asked to listen for at least 30 minutes a day across the eight weeks while viewing the light stimulation, choosing one of the two playlists each day.
The post-intervention session took approximately 7 hours, and participants were compensated $20 per hour.
Compliance measures came from the daily logbooks which participants completed by hand after each session.
Logbook data are incomplete for four participants who completed the intervention and remained in contact with research staff throughout.

We then compared the delta-theta-gamma-driven light stimulation to the delta-driven light stimulation on delta, theta, and gamma gain, and on theta phase-locking value, using a paired cluster-based permutation test across the 30 electrodes, with each participant's values averaged across the two songs (n = 33; one participant had no delta-driven recording for one song and was excluded from these tests).
We asked whether our music and synchronized light stimulus entrained endogenous brain oscillations in our participants.
Participants completed a battery of neuropsychological measures at both sessions, drawn from several instruments rather than from a single published battery.
